statements.statement: The exhaust-color guidance in the HMMWV maintenance manual does not directly specify a diagnostic system for rough-running engines emitting white smoke.

statements.reason: The supplied context does not mention coolant leakage.
statements.statement: According to standard vehicle maintenance knowledge, white exhaust smoke typically indicates coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.

statements.reason: The supplied context does not mention cracked cylinder heads or coolant leakage.
statements.statement: A cracked cylinder head may cause coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.

statements.reason: The supplied context does not mention head gaskets or coolant leakage.
statements.statement: A failed head gasket may cause coolant leakage into the combustion chamber.

statements.reason: The white-exhaust entry directs the reader to fuel-system testing, not an exhaust-color diagnostic system.
statements.statement: The exhaust-color guidance referenced in TM 9-2320-280-20-1 generally directs the maintainer to the exhaust-color diagnostic system for rough running.

evidence_quotes: WHITE. . . . . . . . . .Go to fuel system, Paragraph 2-22. Could be injector timing, DS level fault.

If you are running this test because the engine runs rough remember that air intake and exhaust as
well as internal mechanical problems can also cause this condition.
statements.reason: The white-exhaust entry identifies possible fuel-system faults, and the fuel-system tests explicitly address an engine that runs rough.
statements.statement: According to the exhaust-color diagnostic system, fuel system issues can cause rough running.

statements.reason: Clogged fuel filters are not mentioned.
statements.statement: Clogged fuel filters are an example of a fuel system issue that can cause rough running.

statements.reason: Fuel pump failure is not mentioned.
statements.statement: Fuel pump failure is an example of a fuel system issue that can cause rough running.
According to the exhaust-color diagnostic system, ignition system problems can cause rough running.
Faulty spark plugs are an example of an ignition system problem that can cause rough running.
Faulty ignition coils are an example of an ignition system problem that can cause rough running.
